source_lines.text: boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$

source_lines.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the supplied injective-resolution six-functor construction. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite-type complex algebraic varieties, and let $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ for a field $k$. Write $Y_p=Y\times_X\cdots\times_XY$ with $p+1$ factors, $f_p:Y_p\to X$, and $F_p=f_p^*F$. In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] the natural augmented derived Cech map is a quasi-isomorphism:
$$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Rf_{p*}F_p.$$

Here totalization is the normalized or unnormalized alternating-face total supplied by the simplicial-derived construction. There is one fixed lower cochain bound; consequently its diagonals are finite in every degree. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms. In particular $R\Gamma(X,F)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(Y_p,F_p)$. Individual fibers of $f$ need not be cohomologically acyclic, connected, or smooth.

1.2 The stalk row and one chosen point. Fix $x\in X$ and put $K=F_x$, a complex of $k$-vector spaces with $H^q(K)=H^q(F)_x$; surjectivity of $f$ makes the fiber $S=Y_x$ nonempty. By the proper base change and fiber-pullback clauses of [F1], the stalk at $x$ of $Rf_{p*}F_p$ is $R\Gamma(S^{p+1},K)$ with $K$ the constant derived pullback, and these identifications are natural for all face and degeneracy maps, so the first page of the stalk row in internal degree $q$ is
$$H^q(K)\xrightarrow{\delta_{-1}}H^q(S,K)\xrightarrow{\delta_0}H^q(S^2,K)\xrightarrow{\delta_1}\cdots,$$

where $\delta_p$ is the alternating sum of the pullbacks along the $(p+2)$ coordinate-deletion maps $d_i:S^{p+2}\to S^{p+1}$. Choose one point $y\in S$; no assertion that any positive cohomology group of $S$ vanishes, or that $S$ is connected or smooth, is made or used. [F1, A1, step 1.1]

2.1 Explicit contraction of every augmented row. For $r\geq0$ let $\mathrm{ins}_r:S^r\to S^{r+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate, with $S^0=\mathrm{pt}$; so $\mathrm{ins}_0$ is the point $y$ itself. The deletion and insertion maps satisfy $d_0\,\mathrm{ins}_{r+1}=\mathrm{id}$ and $d_i\,\mathrm{ins}_{r+1}=\mathrm{ins}_r\,d_{i-1}$ for $i>0$. Put $h_{p+1}:=\mathrm{ins}_{p+1}^*:H^q(S^{p+2},K)\to H^q(S^{p+1},K)$ and $h_0:=\mathrm{ins}_0^*:H^q(S,K)\to H^q(K)$, with $\delta_{-1}$ the constant pullback of the projection $S\to\mathrm{pt}$. Applying the two identities termwise gives $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\mathrm{id}$ for every $p\geq0$: the $i=0$ term of $h_{p+1}\delta_p$ is the identity, and the terms $i>0$ are the negatives of $\delta_{p-1}h_p$; moreover $h_0\delta_{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, because the projection followed by the chosen point is the identity of $\mathrm{pt}$. Hence every augmented horizontal row is contractible, in particular exact, in every internal degree $q$, using only functorial pullback on cohomology. [step 1.2, algebra]

candidates.source_claim: For a proper surjection f:Y->X, the augmented derived Cech nerve has Y_p=Y x_X ... x_X Y and F -> Tot_p R f_{p*}F_p. On a stalk, the augmented row is H^q(K)->H^q(S,K)->H^q(S^2,K)->...; insertion of one chosen y in the first coordinate contracts it.

source_lines.text: For a bicosimplicial complex $K^{p,r,q}$ of modules over a commutative ring, with $p,r\geq0$ and one fixed lower bound $q\geq a$, the alternating-face total complex and the diagonal alternating-face total complex are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent:

On the left total degree is $p+r+q$ and differential is $\delta_h+(-1)^p\delta_v+(-1)^{p+r}d$; on the right total degree is $n+q$ and differential is $\delta_{\mathrm{diag}}+(-1)^nd$. These comparisons preserve augmentation and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. They require no dimensional finiteness of the coefficient modules and no choice principle. Normalization can be applied on either side without changing the conclusion.

**Given:** $K^{p,r,q}=0$ unless $p,r\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. Horizontal cofaces $d_h^i:K^{p,r,q}\to K^{p+1,r,q}$ and codegeneracies $s_h^i:K^{p,r,q}\to K^{p-1,r,q}$, and the analogous vertical operators, satisfy the cosimplicial identities and commute between directions. The internal differential raises $q$ by one, squares to zero and commutes with these operators. The three $\delta$'s are the corresponding alternating coface sums. The auxiliary bisimplicial modules in steps 1.1–4.1 instead have faces lowering degree and degeneracies raising it; step 5.1 reverses their universal operator formulas.

1.1 Universal models and contractions. For a bisimplicial $R$-module $M$, let $Q_{p,r}$ have value $R[\Delta([u],[p])\times\Delta([v],[r])]$ at $(u,v)$. An element $x\in M_{p,r}$ determines the unique map $Q_{p,r}\to M$ sending the universal generator to $x$. The diagonal chain complex of $Q_{p,r}$ consists of pairs of monotone vertex strings; define $h$ on each basis string by prepending $(0,0)$. Deleting the first vertex gives the original string, and every other deletion commutes with prepending with its index reduced by one. Thus $\partial h+h\partial=1-e$, where $e$ sends every degree-zero vertex to $(0,0)$ and is zero in positive degrees. On the double total, identified with $C_*(\Delta[p];R)\otimes_R C_*(\Delta[r];R)$, use the separate prepend-zero contractions $h_p,h_r$ and projectors $e_p,e_r$. For homogeneous $x$, set $H(x\otimes y)=h_p(x)\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}e_p(x)\otimes h_r(y)$. The Koszul differential gives $\partial H+H\partial=(1-e_p)\otimes1+e_p\otimes(1-e_r)=1-e_p\otimes e_r$. These contractions fill every positive-degree cycle and every augmentation-zero degree-zero cycle by specified finite chains. Unlike a constant simplicial map on unnormalized chains, $e$ is supported only in degree zero. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 Diagonal-to-total comparison. Put $\operatorname{Diag}_m(M)=M_{m,m}$ and $\operatorname{Tot}_m(M)=\bigoplus_{p+r=m}M_{p,r}$ with the Koszul boundary. Set $\varphi_0=1$. Inductively evaluate $\varphi_{m-1}\partial z$ on the universal generator $z$ of $Q_{m,m}$, and fill it using the total contraction of step 1.1. It is a cycle because $\partial\varphi_{m-1}=\varphi_{m-2}\partial$; when $m=1$, it is the difference of the two endpoint vertices and has augmentation zero. Evaluate that specified filling under the representing map for each $x\in M_{m,m}$ to define $\varphi_m(x)$. This is linear and natural, and its boundary is $\varphi_{m-1}\partial x$. Thus $\varphi$ is a natural chain map, given degreewise by finite linear combinations of structure operators. [step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Total-to-diagonal comparison. Set $\psi_0=1$. For each summand $M_{p,r}$ in total degree $m=p+r>0$, evaluate $\psi_{m-1}\partial z$ on the universal generator of $Q_{p,r}$ and fill it with the diagonal contraction of step 1.1. The induction hypothesis makes it a cycle; in degree $m=1$ its two endpoint coefficients cancel. Evaluate the filling under the representing map of each element of $M_{p,r}$ and sum over $p+r=m$. This defines a linear natural chain map $\psi$, again by specified finite operator formulas. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Homotopy inverses. Let $C,C'$ each be the diagonal or total chain functor, and let $f,g:C\to C'$ be natural chain maps with $f_0=g_0$. Set $h_0=0$. For $m\geq1$, on a universal generator $z$ of a representing summand of $C_m$, put $\beta_m=(f_m-g_m)(z)-h_{m-1}(\partial z)$. The previously established equation $\partial h_{m-1}+h_{m-2}\partial=f_{m-1}-g_{m-1}$ makes $\partial\beta_m=0$. This cycle has positive degree, so its specified model contraction gives $h_m(z)$ with $\partial h_m(z)=\beta_m$. Extend by representing maps. Then $\partial h+h\partial=f-g$. Apply this to $\psi\varphi$ and $1$ on the diagonal, and to $\varphi\psi$ and $1$ on the total; both composites are the identity in degree zero. The resulting natural homotopies have finite operator formulas. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 Cosimplicial variance and the internal differential. The maps and homotopies of steps 2.1–4.1 are finite linear combinations of morphisms in the simplex categories. Their identities can be tested on the free representables of step 1.1, so they are universal additive operator identities. Reverse every operator and every composition to obtain cochain maps in the opposite directions and cochain homotopies lowering simplicial total degree by one. This reverses the two homotopy-inverse identities, without taking algebraic duals. Apply these formulas in each internal degree $q$. Naturality makes them commute with $d$. A comparison preserves simplicial total degree $t=p+r=n$, so it commutes with the signed internal differential $(-1)^td$. For a homotopy $H$ lowering $t$ by one, the internal terms in $DH+HD$ are $(-1)^{t-1}dH+(-1)^tHd=0$. Hence the comparisons and homotopies apply to precisely the two cochain differentials in the Statement. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

source_lines.text: Assume the setup of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]
and the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be the nilpotent cone
with its reduced coordinate ring from
[[lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-reduced-integral-domain]], and let
$\mu:T^*X\to N$ be the Springer moment map. Then $N$ is normal, $\mu$ is
proper and birational, and pullback induces a graded algebra isomorphism
$$\mathbb C[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O_{T^*X}).$$

1.2 The Springer map is $$\mu:G\times^B\mathfrak n^+\longrightarrow N,\qquad[g,x]\longmapsto\operatorname{Ad}(g)x.$$ Its graph is the incidence subvariety $$\{(gB,y)\in X\times N:y\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+\},$$ which is closed because the spaces $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$ form a vector subbundle of $X\times\mathfrak g$. The projection $X\times N\to N$ is projective by [F4], so $\mu$ is proper by the projective-morphism theorem included in [F4]. Surjectivity follows from the last clause of [F1]. [F1, F4]

3.1 The fiber over $e$ is a single point. Indeed, if $e\in\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak n^+$, write $g=b_1n_wb_2$ by [F3]. The element $x=\operatorname{Ad}(b_1^{-1})e$ still has every simple coefficient nonzero by [F2]. Since $\operatorname{Ad}(n_w^{-1})x\in\mathfrak n^+$, each nonzero simple-root component of $x$ must map to a positive root space; distinct root spaces cannot cancel. Therefore $w^{-1}$ sends every positive simple root to a positive root, so $w=1$ by [F3], and $gB=B$. This algebraic argument holds after every algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb C$ as well. Equivariance gives a singleton geometric fiber over every point of $O=G\cdot e$. The restriction $\mu_O:\mu^{-1}(O)\to O$ is proper by base change. Its fibers are finite type and their geometric point sets are singletons, so each fiber point is isolated and has residue field finite over the base residue field; the finite-fiber criterion in [F8] makes $\mu_O$ quasi-finite, and proper quasi-finite finiteness in [F8] makes it finite. Both source and target are integral of dimension $2|\Phi^+|$, so the induced function-field extension is finite. It is separable in characteristic zero, and by [F9] has a primitive element $\theta$. After replacing an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq O$ by a smaller nonempty principal open, its finite preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $A$, $\theta$ lies in $B$, and $B=A[\theta]\cong A[T]/(f)$ for the monic minimal polynomial $f$ of $\theta$: first clear denominators to place $\theta$ in $B$, then localize to kill the finite torsion quotient $B/A[\theta]$ and to put the coefficients of $f$ in $A$. The discriminant of $f$ is nonzero by separability, so after inverting it this finite map is étale of rank $d=[\operatorname{Frac}B:\operatorname{Frac}A]$. Every geometric closed fiber in this open then has $d$ distinct points, but every geometric fiber over $O$ is a singleton; therefore $d=1$. This proves birationality without inferring degree from a closed-point count alone. [F2, F3, F8, F9, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2]
